evidence.note: Large diagram panel is completely empty at the opening step; the slide reads as a title, steps list and a blank card.

Finished diagram is three plain boxes in a vertical line with arrows (Return request, Warehouse, Refund); it repeats the step list and shows nothing of the three-versus-eleven-days claim, leaving much of the panel empty.
'Median days, January to March, all regions' caption sits far below the steps list with no chart or figure it captions.
Quote tiles stack cleanly in the right column, each with a consistent uppercase label and serif quote; nothing collides.
Short-wide layout reflows cleanly: steps, diagram and tiles fit without overlap; caption wraps to two lines beside the diagram card.
Step markers and text treatments are consistent (active green, done dark, pending outline); typography is coherent across eyebrow, title, body and quotes.

rationale: Styling is consistent and clean at both sizes with no collisions or clutter, so it clears levels 1 and 2. But the diagram is a generic three-box chain that duplicates the step list, leaves its panel largely empty and does not show the headline comparison, with an orphaned data caption, so it does not reach the reference bar. That matches level 3: consistent and clean, but generic, with the diagram not yet doing its job.
